_readme: WP3 golden sample. HAND-VERIFIED expected values, used by scraper/harness_cisco_specs.ts to
gate the extractor at >=98% field-exact precision before any bulk write (STOP condition 2).
How these were verified, because the distinction matters: each entry records the RAW cell
string as it appears in the datasheet and the expected NORMALISED value, and the arithmetic
between them was checked by hand. e.g. '1.73 x 17.5 x 16.1' under a label saying inches must
become 43.942 x 444.5 x 408.94 mm (x25.4); '208 Gbps' must become 208 Gbit/s; '299,000' under
an English-locale sheet must become 299000, NOT 299.0.
Expected values were NOT copied from the extractor's own output and blessed - that would be a
tautology that passes no matter how wrong the pipeline is. The harness additionally runs a
PROVENANCE AUDIT: for every fact the pipeline emits it re-opens the cached HTML, rebuilds the
grid, walks to the recorded locator (table/row/column) and asserts the raw string is really
in that cell. That checks the extractor at full scale, not just on this sample.
Coverage [M 2026-09-01]: 46 fields across 12 PIDs from 6 of the 10 golden datasheets. The
other 4 (Catalyst 1000, 1300, 2960-L, and most of 9500) publish their specifications at
SERIES level - columns read '48-port models (1/10G uplinks)', not part numbers - so they
yield no per-SKU values to verify. That is a property of Cisco's documents, not a gap in the
sample, and it is why family inheritance (Q5) is the only route to per-SKU depth there.
HELD BACK 2026-09-01: poe_budget, power_typical and power_max were removed from the
expectations (46 -> 26) and preserved under `held_back`.
They were extracted correctly from the cells named, but those tables are keyed by a
CONFIGURATION the schema cannot yet record: table 3 lists C9300-24P twice (445W PoE with the
default 715W PSU, 720W with the upgrade 1100W PSU) and the power table's 'Measured P(W)'
columns are HALF-port traffic with a separate full-port column, repeated per input voltage.
The expectations are kept here so they can be restored verbatim once the parser captures the
qualifier - they are evidence of what the cells say, not of what the field should hold.

CORRECTED 2026-09-04: the psu_options entries for C9300-24P and C9300-24U each held ONE CELL of a list the datasheet spreads over several cells (a 'Default AC power supply' column in the model table plus one 'Primary power supply' row per configuration in the PSU table). The extractor now joins the cells of one table and the apply unions an `ls` field one document states twice, so the expected value is the FULL list in document order, read from the cached datasheets by hand. UNCHANGED, and each for its own reason: C9200CX-8P-2X2G's two cells are identical, so they corroborate rather than extend; C9200CX-12P-2X2G's second cell sits under 'Default primary power supply', a label no alias rule matches, so the datasheet's other spelling of the same 315W supply is an unmapped label and NOT part of what the pipeline can state (recorded in the unmapped report, not blessed into a golden); WS-C3850-48P and -48F have one power-supply cell each.
